1.label: ТЕКСТ
1.title: How It All Began
1.q: Прочитай текст і дай відповіді на питання.
1.q_pl: Przeczytaj tekst i odpowiedz na pytania.
1.q_en: Read the text and answer the questions.
1.text:
In the spring of 2005, Ted Mosby was sitting in his apartment when his best friend Marshall came home with a ring box. He had been planning the proposal for weeks, and by the end of the evening Lily had said yes. While the happy couple were celebrating, Ted suddenly realised that he wanted the same thing.

That same night, at the bar downstairs, he noticed a young reporter called Robin. He had never believed in love at first sight, but he walked over and introduced himself. After a perfect evening in her apartment, he did something unforgivable: he told her he was in love with her.

Robin laughed nervously. She had just moved to New York, and the last thing she wanted was a serious relationship. Ted walked home alone, convinced he had ruined everything.

words.d: a romantic connection between two people

items.q: What did Ted say that ruined the evening?
options: That he was in love with Robin

items.q: Why didn't Robin want anything serious?
options: She had just moved to New York

items.q: Which sentence uses the past perfect continuous?
options: He has planned the proposal last week.
He was plan the proposal for weeks.
He had been planning the proposal for weeks.

items.q: Which sentence shows an action in progress interrupted?
options: Ted has sat at home when Marshall came.
Ted sat at home when Marshall had come in.
Ted was sitting at home when Marshall came in.

2.label: ТЕКСТ
2.title: The Third Party
2.q: Прочитай текст і дай відповіді на питання.
2.q_pl: Przeczytaj tekst i odpowiedz na pytania.
2.q_en: Read the text and answer the questions.
2.text:
Ted has been trying to see Robin again for two weeks, and he has come up with a plan that is far from subtle. He has organised a party, then another, and then a third, each time hoping that she will 'just happen' to drop by.

His friends have been patient, but they are running out of energy. Marshall and Lily have been hiding on the roof for most of the evening, and the guests have eaten everything in the fridge. Ted has even carried a giant purple stuffed giraffe across the city, simply because Robin once mentioned that she liked one.

When Robin finally arrives, she has already guessed what is going on. 'Have you been throwing these parties for me?' she asks. Ted, who has never been good at lying, admits that he has.

items.q: Where are Marshall and Lily hiding?
Which sentence uses the present perfect continuous?
options: Ted tried to see her for two weeks now.
Ted has been trying to see her for two weeks.
Ted is trying to see her since two weeks.

items.q: Which sentence focuses on a finished result?
options: He has been organising three parties.

3.label: ТЕКСТ
3.title: The Legendary Night
3.q: Прочитай текст і дай відповіді на питання.
3.q_pl: Przeczytaj tekst i odpowiedz na pytania.
3.q_en: Read the text and answer the questions.
3.text:
Barney has decided that tonight is going to be legendary. 'We're not going to MacLaren's,' he announces. 'We're meeting two women at the airport at eight, and their flight leaves at nine.' The women are flying to Philadelphia, so Barney is going to buy two tickets and follow them.

Ted is not sure this is a good idea. 'What will we do if they don't like us?' he asks. Barney only smiles. 'You'll see. I'll handle everything.'

Of course, nothing goes according to plan. They get past security but miss the flight, and they end up spending the night in the airport, being questioned about Barney's strange behaviour. At dawn they sit on a bench eating stale doughnuts. 'Next weekend,' Barney says, 'we're going to Las Vegas.' Ted has no doubt that he means it.

items.q: What does Barney plan for next weekend?

options: Their flight will left at nine.
Their flight is going to leave yesterday.

items.q: Which sentence is a spontaneous promise?

4.label: ТЕКСТ
4.title: The Shirt
4.q: Прочитай текст і дай відповіді на питання.
4.q_pl: Przeczytaj tekst i odpowiedz na pytania.
4.q_en: Read the text and answer the questions.
4.text:
When Ted found the shirt at the back of his closet, he immediately thought of Natalie. He must have left it at her place years ago, he reasoned, and she must have kept it all this time. 'It can't be a coincidence,' he told his friends. 'She might still have feelings for me.'

His friends were less sure. 'It could be the wrong shirt,' Robin pointed out. 'Or she may have given it back simply because she was tidying up.'

Ted called Natalie anyway, and within a week they were dating again. It took him exactly seven days to remember why he had broken up with her. The problem was that he had already dumped her once, on her birthday, by answering machine. Doing it again was going to be much harder.

words.d: a device that records phone messages

items.q: What did Ted find in his closet?
How did Ted break up with Natalie the first time?
options: By answering machine on her birthday

items.q: How long did it take Ted to remember the problem?

options: It couldn't to be a coincidence.

5.label: ТЕКСТ
5.title: The Slutty Pumpkin
5.q: Прочитай текст і дай відповіді на питання.
5.q_pl: Przeczytaj tekst i odpowiedz na pytania.
5.q_en: Read the text and answer the questions.
5.text:
Every Halloween, Ted would put on the same costume and go to the same rooftop party. His friends used to laugh at him, but they had got used to it by now. Years earlier, he had spent a whole night talking to a girl dressed as a pumpkin. She wrote her number on a sweet wrapper, and he lost it before he got home.

Since then, Ted had been waiting for her to come back. 'I'm used to being disappointed,' he would say, 'but this year feels different.'

This year, incredibly, she did come back. They talked, they laughed, and they discovered that they had absolutely nothing in common. The perfect girl from his memory was, in reality, just a nice stranger. Ted went home early and never wore that costume again.

words.d: special clothes to look like someone else
sad because something was not as good as expected
a person you do not know

items.q: Where did Ted meet the pumpkin girl?
Where did she write her number?
What did they discover when they met again?

options: special clothes to look like someone else

items.q: Which sentence describes a past habit?
options: Ted would to put on the same costume.
Ted is used to put on the same costume.
Ted would put on the same costume.

7.label: ТЕКСТ
7.title: Okay Awesome
7.q: Прочитай текст і дай відповіді на питання.
7.q_pl: Przeczytaj tekst i odpowiedz na pytania.
7.q_en: Read the text and answer the questions.
7.text:
Marshall and Lily have decided they are grown-ups now. Instead of going to a club, they invite friends for a quiet evening of cheese and wine. Meanwhile Ted, Barney and Robin are queuing outside the hottest club in town.

Inside, the music is so loud that nobody can hear anything, so people just shout 'Okay, awesome!' at each other. Robin hates it. 'If I were at home, I would be asleep by now,' she says. Ted agrees: 'If this place were any louder, my ears would explode.'

Back at the apartment, Lily feels the same way about the cheese party. 'If we were at the club,' she whispers, 'we would be dancing.' By midnight, everyone has swapped places: Marshall and Lily are dancing in the club, while Robin and Ted sit at home, eating the leftover cheese and enjoying the silence.

items.q: What do Marshall and Lily organise?
options: A quiet cheese and wine evening
The music is too loud to hear

items.q: Where are Robin and Ted at midnight?
Which sentence is a correct second conditional?
options: If I were at home, I will be asleep.
If I were at home, I would be asleep.
If I am at home, I would be asleep.

items.q: Which sentence describes an imaginary present situation?
options: If we were at the club, we would be dancing.
If we are at the club, we dance.
If we had been at the club, we danced.

8.label: ТЕКСТ
8.title: The Perfect Match
8.q: Прочитай текст і дай відповіді на питання.
8.q_pl: Przeczytaj tekst i odpowiedz na pytania.
8.q_en: Read the text and answer the questions.
8.text:
Ted paid a matchmaker a small fortune to find his perfect partner. Her computer analysed thousands of profiles and, to everyone's surprise, found nobody. 'If you hadn't been so picky,' Barney said, 'we would have found someone by now.' Ted was crushed.

The matchmaker herself was confused. 'If the system had worked properly, it would have given us at least ten names,' she admitted. She promised to call him the moment anyone suitable appeared.

A few weeks later, she did. Ted rushed to the office, his heart racing. 'There's one woman,' the matchmaker said, 'and she's absolutely perfect for you.' Future Ted pauses at this point in the story. 'Kids, if I had met her that day, you would have heard a very different story. But she wasn't your mother.'

words.d: a person who finds partners for others

items.q: What did the computer find at first?
What does Future Ted say about the woman?
Which sentence is a correct third conditional?
options: If you hadn't been so picky, we will find someone.
If you hadn't been so picky, we would have found someone.
If you weren't so picky, we would have find someone.

items.q: Choose the correct form: 'If the system had worked, it ___ ten names.'

9.label: ТЕКСТ
9.title: Thanksgiving in Minnesota
9.q: Прочитай текст і дай відповіді на питання.
9.q_pl: Przeczytaj tekst i odpowiedz na pytania.
9.q_en: Read the text and answer the questions.
9.text:
Marshall's family in Minnesota are all enormous, cheerful people who hug constantly and play basketball after every meal. Lily, who is tiny and from New York, feels completely out of place. 'I wish I could play basketball,' she sighs. 'If only they didn't keep staring at me.'

It gets worse when she accidentally reveals that she doesn't believe in the family's favourite tradition. Marshall's mother goes silent. Lily wishes she had kept her mouth shut.

Meanwhile, in New York, Ted and Robin are volunteering at a homeless shelter. Robin wishes she had a family to go home to; Ted wishes he could think of something comforting to say. At midnight, both couples talk on the phone. 'If only we were all together at the bar,' Lily says, and for once, everyone agrees.

words.d: a custom passed down over time
a place that gives protection to people in need

items.q: How does Lily feel in Minnesota?
Which sentence expresses a regret about the past?
options: Lily wishes she kept her mouth shut tomorrow.
Lily wishes she had kept her mouth shut.
Lily wishes she will keep her mouth shut.

items.q: Which sentence expresses a wish about the present?
options: If only we were all together.
If only we are all together.
If only we will be together.

10.label: ТЕКСТ
10.title: The Morning After
10.q: Прочитай текст і дай відповіді на питання.
10.q_pl: Przeczytaj tekst i odpowiedz na pytania.
10.q_en: Read the text and answer the questions.
10.text:
Ted woke up with a burn on his hand, a pineapple on his bedside table and a woman he had never met asleep in his bed. He remembered absolutely nothing.

One by one, his friends filled in the gaps. Barney said Ted had claimed he could drink five cocktails in a row. Marshall said that Ted had told everyone he was going to call Robin. Lily added that he had actually called her, three times, and that he had tried to sing to her answering machine.

The burn, Robin explained, came from a dare involving a lighter and the fireplace. The woman in the bed turned out to be a friend of a friend, who said she had only needed somewhere to sleep. But the pineapple remained a mystery. Nobody ever found out where it had come from.

words.d: a challenge to do something risky

items.q: What did Ted find on his bedside table?
How many times did Ted call Robin?

options: a challenge to do something risky
He claimed I could drink five cocktails.
He claimed he can drank five cocktails.
He claimed he could drink five cocktails.
He said I was going to call Robin.
He said he was going to call Robin.
He said he is go to call Robin.

11.label: ТЕКСТ
11.title: New Year's Eve in a Limo
11.title_pl: New Year's Eve in a Limo
11.title_en: New Year's Eve in a Limo
11.q: Прочитай текст і дай відповіді на питання.
11.q_pl: Przeczytaj tekst i odpowiedz na pytania.
11.q_en: Read the text and answer the questions.
11.text:
Ted's plan had been carefully prepared for weeks. A limousine was rented, five parties were chosen, and a schedule was printed for everyone. By midnight, he promised, every party would have been visited.

Unfortunately, nothing went as planned. Robin's date was left behind at the second party, Barney was thrown out of the third, and the driver was given so much advice that he stopped listening completely. Then the limo was trapped in traffic on Fifth Avenue.

With minutes to go before midnight, Ted realised that the best part of the evening had already happened: the five of them laughing in the back of a car. The countdown was heard on the radio. At midnight, they kissed, hugged and opened warm champagne. The parties, everyone agreed, had been completely unnecessary.

words.d: a plan of times for activities
keep someone in a place they cannot leave

options: The best part had already happened

items.q: Which sentence uses the passive correctly?
Which sentence uses the present perfect passive?
options: The plan has been carefully prepared.

13.label: ТЕКСТ
13.title: The Woman Who Made the Cake
13.title_pl: The Woman Who Made the Cake
13.title_en: The Woman Who Made the Cake
13.q: Прочитай текст і дай відповіді на питання.
13.q_pl: Przeczytaj tekst i odpowiedz na pytania.
13.q_en: Read the text and answer the questions.
13.text:
Ted went to the wedding alone, because the woman he had been seeing had just left him. It was there that he met Victoria, a baker whose cakes were famous across the city. She was the one who had made the enormous wedding cake that everyone was admiring.

They danced, they laughed, and they agreed on one strange rule: they would not tell each other their names. 'Let it be one magical night,' she said, 'which we'll always remember.'

At the end of the evening, standing at the place where the guests were collecting their coats, Victoria kissed him and disappeared. Ted, who rarely does anything spontaneous, regretted the rule immediately. He spent the following week trying to find a woman whose name he didn't know, using only a slice of cake as evidence.

words.d: feel sorry about something you did
a thin piece cut from something

items.q: What rule did they agree on?
options: Not to tell each other their names
a thin piece cut from something

items.q: Choose the correct relative pronoun: 'a baker ___ cakes were famous'
Choose the correct relative pronoun: 'the place ___ the guests collected their coats'

14.label: ТЕКСТ
14.title: Finding Victoria
14.q: Прочитай текст і дай відповіді на питання.
14.q_pl: Przeczytaj tekst i odpowiedz na pytania.
14.q_en: Read the text and answer the questions.
14.text:
Ted can't stop thinking about Victoria. He tries to forget her, but every time he passes a bakery, he stops to look in the window. Lily decides that enough is enough. She calls the bride, finds out the name of the bakery and makes Ted go there.

'I'm terrible at starting conversations like this,' Ted panics outside the door. 'I keep imagining her laughing at me.' Lily refuses to listen. 'Stop complaining and go in.'

When he finally walks in, Victoria is decorating a cake. She looks up, recognises him and smiles. Ted forgets to say hello. He remembers practising a clever line all the way there, but now he can't remember a single word. Fortunately, Victoria doesn't seem to mind. She offers him a cupcake and agrees to have dinner with him on Friday.

words.d: a shop that sells bread and cakes
know someone you have seen before

items.q: What is Victoria doing when Ted enters?
What happens with Ted's clever line?
'He stops to look in the window' means…
options: he pauses in order to look
he said hello and forgot it

15.label: ТЕКСТ
15.title: Embarrassing Stories
15.q: Прочитай текст і дай відповіді на питання.
15.q_pl: Przeczytaj tekst i odpowiedz na pytania.
15.q_en: Read the text and answer the questions.
15.text:
Game night at Ted's apartment was going badly until Lily came up with a new game: everyone had to tell their most embarrassing story. Ted went first, then Marshall, then Robin. Barney tried to get out of it, but the others wouldn't let him off.

Finally he gave in. Years ago, it turned out, Barney had been a completely different person: he wore sweaters, played the guitar and planned to join the Peace Corps with his girlfriend. Then she broke up with him for a man in a suit. Barney picked himself up, cut off his long hair and put on his first suit.

The room went silent. Nobody knew what to say. Then Barney looked at their faces and burst out laughing. 'Got you,' he said. Nobody could work out whether the story was true.

words.d: not punish or not make someone do something

items.q: Whose idea was the new game?
Why did Barney's girlfriend leave him?
options: For a man in a suit

items.q: What couldn't the friends work out?

16.label: ТЕКСТ
16.title: Suits and Dresses
16.q: Прочитай текст і дай відповіді на питання.
16.q_pl: Przeczytaj tekst i odpowiedz na pytania.
16.q_en: Read the text and answer the questions.
16.text:
Lily has found the perfect wedding dress, but it costs more than her car. Instead, she decides to have her grandmother's old dress altered. The tailor promises to have it ready in three weeks.

Meanwhile, Marshall needs a suit for his first job interview. He wants to buy something cheap off the rack, but Barney is horrified. 'You have to get a suit made to measure,' he insists. 'Nobody gets hired in a suit that doesn't fit.' He takes Marshall to his own tailor and has him measured from head to toe.

And then there is Victoria. A famous chef has offered her a place on a pastry course in Germany. She hasn't decided yet, but she has had her passport renewed, just in case. Ted pretends not to notice.

words.d: a person who makes or repairs clothes

items.q: What has Victoria done just in case?

options: a person who makes or repairs clothes

items.q: Choose the correct causative: 'Barney had Marshall ___.'

17.label: ТЕКСТ
17.title: The Law Firm
17.q: Прочитай текст і дай відповіді на питання.
17.q_pl: Przeczytaj tekst i odpowiedz na pytania.
17.q_en: Read the text and answer the questions.
17.text:
Marshall spent the summer as an intern at a big corporate law firm. The pay was excellent, but the atmosphere was terrible: the partners shouted at everyone, and the other interns behaved like gorillas fighting over bananas. Marshall had always dreamed of protecting the environment.

When he decided not to return, Barney was disgusted. 'If you had stayed, you would be rich now,' he said. Marshall shrugged. 'If I were the kind of person who could stay there, I would have stayed.'

Lily supported him completely, although she secretly worried about money. 'If he hadn't left,' she told Robin, 'we would be able to afford a better apartment. But if he were happy there, he wouldn't be Marshall.' Future Ted adds: 'And kids, that was the first time I realised how much Marshall cared about doing the right thing.'

words.d: a student who works to get experience

19.label: ТЕКСТ
19.title: Two A.M.
19.q: Прочитай текст і дай відповіді на питання.
19.q_pl: Przeczytaj tekst i odpowiedz na pytania.
19.q_en: Read the text and answer the questions.
19.text:
Victoria is in Germany, and Ted is trying hard to make long-distance work. It isn't easy, is it? At two in the morning his phone rings. It's Robin. 'You're not asleep, are you?' she asks. 'You'd like to come over, wouldn't you?'

Ted's mother always told him that nothing good happens after two a.m. He knows she was right, doesn't he? Yet twenty minutes later, he is standing outside Robin's door, arguing with himself. 'It's just a friendly visit, isn't it? Nobody would mind, would they?'

Future Ted interrupts the story. 'Kids, I'd love to tell you I went home. But I didn't, did I? And that was the night I learned that the right answer and the easy answer are rarely the same.' He sighs. 'Your grandmother was right about two a.m., wasn't she?'

words.d: try to decide between two choices
stop someone while they are speaking

items.q: What did Ted's mother always say?
Where is Ted standing at the end?
Choose the correct tag: 'You're not asleep, ___?'
Choose the correct tag: 'Nobody would mind, ___?'

20.label: ТЕКСТ
20.title: The Phone Call
20.q: Прочитай текст і дай відповіді на питання.
20.q_pl: Przeczytaj tekst i odpowiedz na pytania.
20.q_en: Read the text and answer the questions.
20.text:
Ted shouldn't have gone to Robin's apartment that night. When his phone rang, Robin answered it before he could stop her. 'It was your girlfriend,' she said slowly. Ted had never told Robin that he was still with Victoria, and Victoria broke up with him over the phone.

The next day, his friends explained what he should have done. 'You should have told Robin the truth,' Lily said. 'You could have stayed home,' added Marshall. Barney thought Ted needn't have apologised to anyone, which helped nobody.

Ted knew they were right. He could have called Victoria first; he should have been honest with both women. Future Ted is quiet for a moment. 'Kids, I could have saved myself a lot of pain that year. But at least I learned something.'

items.q: How did Victoria end the relationship?
What did Lily say Ted should have done?
Which sentence criticises a past action?
options: You must told her the truth.
You should have told her the truth.

21.label: ТЕКСТ
21.title: The Prom Band
21.q: Прочитай текст і дай відповіді на питання.
21.q_pl: Przeczytaj tekst i odpowiedz na pytania.
21.q_en: Read the text and answer the questions.
21.text:
Marshall and Lily have been looking for a wedding band for months, and they have finally found the perfect one, playing at a high school prom. To hear them properly, the whole group sneaks into the dance, pretending to be chaperones.

Lily has planned everything. 'This time next year, we'll be dancing to this exact song at our wedding,' she tells Marshall. 'By June, we'll have booked the band, and by the summer, we'll have sent all the invitations.'

Unfortunately, the band is not for hire: the singer is still at school. Lily is devastated, but Marshall just smiles. 'In ten years,' he says, 'we won't remember the band. We'll be remembering tonight.' Ted, watching them dance in a gym full of teenagers, thinks it might be the most romantic thing he has ever seen.

an adult who watches young people at an event
available to be paid for work

22.label: ТЕКСТ
22.title: The Fellowship
22.q: Прочитай текст і дай відповіді на питання.
22.q_pl: Przeczytaj tekst i odpowiedz na pytania.
22.q_en: Read the text and answer the questions.
22.text:
It was Lily who saw the advertisement first: a summer art fellowship in San Francisco. What she wanted, more than anything, was to apply. What she feared was what Marshall would say. So she applied in secret.

Then Marshall's car got a flat tyre on the way to a family dinner, and Lily had to call Ted for help. It was during that long, cold wait by the road that she told him everything. Ted promised to keep quiet.

What worried Lily most was not the application itself but the question behind it. Did she want to be married at twenty-seven, or did she want to be an artist first? 'It's not Marshall I'm unsure about,' she told Ted. 'It's me.' Ted had no answer. All he could do was hand her his coat.

words.d: a paid position for study or research
formally ask for a job or place

options: The car got a flat tyre
It was Lily who saw the advertisement first.
What she feared was Marshall's reaction.

23.label: ТЕКСТ
23.title: Opposites (A Flash-Forward)
23.q: Прочитай текст і дай відповіді на питання.
23.q_pl: Przeczytaj tekst i odpowiedz na pytania.
23.q_en: Read the text and answer the questions.
23.text:
Future Ted jumps ahead: 'A few months later, Robin and I were finally together.' Although they are very different, they are surprisingly good together. Robin loves hockey and the shooting range, whereas Ted prefers architecture and poetry.

Despite their differences, they laugh at the same jokes. Ted drags Robin to a museum; in spite of her complaints, she ends up enjoying it. In return, Robin takes Ted to a hockey game. Even though he understands nothing, he cheers louder than anyone.

However, not everything is easy. Robin hates talking about the future, while Ted can't stop planning it. 'But that comes later, kids,' Future Ted says. 'Back in the spring of 2006, Robin and I were still just friends, and I was still trying to work out what I really wanted.'

words.d: a place where people practise shooting
make someone go somewhere they don't want to
a statement that you are unhappy

25.label: ТЕКСТ
25.title: The Interview
25.q: Прочитай текст і дай відповіді на питання.
25.q_pl: Przeczytaj tekst i odpowiedz na pytania.
25.q_en: Read the text and answer the questions.
25.text:
Lily secretly travelled to the interview for the art fellowship. The panel was polite but serious. They asked her why she wanted to spend the summer in San Francisco, and whether she was ready to leave New York for three months.

Back home, she told Robin everything. 'They asked if I had ever exhibited my work. They wanted to know who had influenced me most.' One of the judges, she added, had told her to bring more paintings next time. Another had asked her not to be so modest.

Robin asked her whether she had told Marshall yet. Lily went pale. 'Not yet,' she admitted. Robin told her to tell him soon, before he found out from someone else. Lily promised she would, but she asked Robin not to say anything to Ted.

not talking about your own abilities

26.label: ТЕКСТ
26.title: Getting Used to Each Other (A Flash-Forward)
26.title_pl: Getting Used to Each Other (A Flash-Forward)
26.title_en: Getting Used to Each Other (A Flash-Forward)
26.q: Прочитай текст і дай відповіді на питання.
26.q_pl: Przeczytaj tekst i odpowiedz na pytania.
26.q_en: Read the text and answer the questions.
26.text:
Future Ted jumps ahead again: 'That summer, Robin and I were getting used to each other.' Robin isn't used to someone making her breakfast; she used to eat cereal standing over the sink. Ted isn't used to five dogs jumping on the bed at six in the morning.

'You'll get used to it,' Robin promises. Ted isn't so sure. He used to sleep until nine at weekends, and now he is woken by barking.

Slowly, though, they adjust. Robin gets used to Ted reading poetry aloud. Ted gets used to dog hair on everything he owns. 'But that comes later, kids,' Future Ted says. 'First, I had to survive the spring.'

a breakfast food made from grain

a basin with taps in a kitchen

27.title: The Rules

Ted points out that he doesn't need rules: he is perfectly happy as he is. Barney looks horrified. 'You'd better not repeat that in public.'

Meanwhile, Lily and Marshall are discussing the wedding. 'I'd rather have a small wedding,' Lily says. 'I'd prefer to invite only family.' Marshall frowns. 'I'd rather we invited everyone. It's time my family met yours.' They argue for an hour and finally agree on a compromise: a medium-sized wedding, with a very long guest list.

28.label: ТЕКСТ
28.title: The Painting
28.q: Прочитай текст і дай відповіді на питання.
28.q_pl: Przeczytaj tekst i odpowiedz na pytania.

28.text:
Having signed up for an evening painting class, Lily discovered that art meant more to her than she had ever admitted. Working late every night, she finished her first serious canvas in two weeks.

Carrying it home on the subway, she felt nervous and proud at the same time. Shown to her friends that evening, the painting impressed everyone, even Barney. 'Painted by Lily Aldrin,' Marshall announced, 'future famous artist.'

Her teacher was equally enthusiastic. 'You should think about applying for something bigger,' she said, handing Lily a leaflet about the San Francisco fellowship. Folding it carefully, Lily put it in her bag. Not having told Marshall about it, she felt a small knot of guilt in her stomach all evening.

words.d: a feeling of having done wrong

29.label: ТЕКСТ
29.title: The Best Man Contest

Marshall has to choose a best man, and both Ted and Barney want the job. To settle it, they agree to a speech contest. Barney begins grandly: 'Never in my life have I seen a couple more perfect than this one.'

Ted answers immediately. 'Not only is Marshall my best friend, but Lily is like a sister to me. Rarely does anyone find love this young, and never have two people deserved it more.'

Barney fights back: 'Seldom has a man been so loyal. Only after years of friendship did I realise what Marshall truly means to me.' The speeches go on for an hour. In the end, Marshall chooses Ted, but he makes Barney a 'best man in training'. Little did Barney know that he would mention this title for years.

31.title: The Rain Dance
31.q: Прочитай текст і дай відповіді на питання.
31.q_pl: Przeczytaj tekst i odpowiedz na pytania.
31.q_en: Read the text and answer the questions.
31.text:
Robin is going camping for the weekend with Sandy Rivers, her handsome co-anchor, and Ted is worried. 'Could you tell me what the forecast says?' he asks Marshall. 'I wonder if it might rain.' It won't, Marshall replies: sunshine all weekend.

So Ted goes up to the roof and performs a rain dance. Barney laughs at him at first, then joins in. 'Do you know whether this has ever worked?' he asks. Ted admits he has no idea.

Twenty minutes later, the sky turns black, and it pours. The camping trip is cancelled. Robin, soaked, comes over to the apartment instead. 'Do you have any idea why the forecast was so wrong?' she asks. Ted and Barney exchange a look and say nothing.

32.label: ТЕКСТ
32.title: The Truth Comes Out
32.q: Прочитай текст і дай відповіді на питання.
32.q_pl: Przeczytaj tekst i odpowiedz na pytania.
32.q_en: Read the text and answer the questions.
32.text:
Lily was going to tell Marshall that evening. She had promised herself she would. She was about to start speaking when Marshall proudly showed her the wedding invitations, which he had printed himself and decorated with tiny hearts.

She couldn't do it. 'I was going to tell him,' she cried to Robin later. 'I was just about to open my mouth, and then he smiled at me.'

In the end, Marshall found out the worst possible way: from a letter of acceptance from San Francisco, which arrived while Lily was out. He sat at the kitchen table reading it again and again. When Lily walked in, she knew at once that she would never have to explain. Future Ted: 'Kids, the truth always comes out. The only question is who tells it.'

33.label: ТЕКСТ
33.title: Rain on the Steps
33.q: Прочитай текст і дай відповіді на питання.
33.q_pl: Przeczytaj tekst i odpowiedz na pytania.
33.q_en: Read the text and answer the questions.
33.text:
Lily has decided to go to San Francisco. The conversation with Marshall is so painful that Ted leaves the room. 'I'm too young not to try,' Lily says quietly. 'And I'm not strong enough to let you go,' Marshall replies.

She leaves that night with such a small suitcase that it seems she will be back by morning. She isn't.

Ted comes home late to find Marshall sitting on the front steps in the pouring rain, holding the ring. It is so cold that Ted can see his breath. He doesn't say anything; there aren't enough words for a moment like this. He just sits down next to his best friend and stays there until the rain stops. Future Ted: 'Kids, sometimes being there is enough.'

34.label: ТЕКСТ
34.title: Future Ted's Lesson
34.q: Прочитай текст і дай відповіді на питання.
34.q_pl: Przeczytaj tekst i odpowiedz na pytania.
34.q_en: Read the text and answer the questions.
34.text:
It is the end of the season. Marshall is alone, Lily is in San Francisco, and Robin and Ted are trying to decide what comes next. Future Ted turns to his children.

'If you want something, you fight for it. If you don't take risks, you never find out what you could have had. If I were your age again, I would be braver. If I had known then what I know now, I would have done everything differently.'

He pauses. 'But if I had done everything differently, I wouldn't be sitting here with you today.' The kids look at each other. 'So, Dad,' his daughter asks, 'are you ever going to tell us how you met Mom?' Ted smiles. 'If you're patient,' he says, 'you'll find out.'
